scoring: Equal task weight. A task earns one point only after all five evidence dimensions pass: outcome, role/data scope, interaction/navigation, status/recovery, desktop/mobile/accessibility. Unsupported or unverified tasks earn no verified point. No implementation score is asserted by this research.
scope: Documented public workflows relevant to Etail; not 90% of all Amex products, private internals or brand pixels. Architecture uses separate mandatory gates.

workflows.journey: Select the intended account or card
workflows.acceptance: Selection persists through reload and is visible in every action review; revoked selection asks for a new choice.

workflows.journey: Give an additional holder an individual login
workflows.acceptance: The invited holder uses their own identity and sees only authorized activity; sponsorship does not create another fee.
A role summary lists action and resource grants; administrative status does not imply spending or payout authority.
The invitation previews exact permitted actions and resources; the grant cannot exceed the sender's delegable ceiling.
Subsequent reads, exports and commands deny revoked scope while retaining auditable historical actions.

workflows.journey: Assign a card to an authorized participant
workflows.acceptance: The assignment names the holder and resource; adding visibility cannot issue a new card or create backing.
The hierarchy shows only approved Seller relationships; a reporting group is not a new account type or liability.
Authorized location access is explicit and adding a location cannot confer merchant ownership.
The product names the responsible party and holder separately without exposing unrelated Personal balances.

workflows.journey: Set or change a spending limit
workflows.acceptance: The review shows ceiling, usage and effective period; changing a limit cannot restore consumed capacity.

workflows.journey: Pause and resume permitted card activity
workflows.acceptance: Effective versus pending restriction is visible; a child unfreeze never overrides a parent restriction.
The UI explains merchant classification and labels alert-only behavior; it never promises basket-level blocking.
The chosen threshold/channel persists; delivery retries do not create financial effects or leak revoked scope.
A fresh purpose-bound step-up is checked on submit; stale verification cannot authorize a changed payload.
Only an explicit payer grant can schedule a permitted obligation payment; generic Manager status is insufficient.

workflows.journey: Separate bank-setting authority from payer authority
workflows.acceptance: Destination changes and execution use independent capabilities; in-flight instructions retain their reviewed destination.
Authentication, operational notifications and marketing consent are distinguished; verified change status is visible.

workflows.journey: Review people with access to a merchant
workflows.acceptance: The audit lists current authorized grants and location scope; export enforces the same scope as the screen.

workflows.journey: Start a card application in context
workflows.acceptance: All entry points open one saved request with selected account and server-provided prerequisites.
Server checks person, accepted relationship, product and funding assignment; tampered identifiers fail.
Draft and request identity survive refresh/session recovery; a stale version reports a recoverable conflict.

workflows.journey: Ask an applicant to complete their part
workflows.acceptance: A scoped applicant task exposes only required fields; expiry or revocation leaves the original request intact.
Existing relationship data is reviewed and versioned; edits cannot mutate someone else's identity record.
Consent references the exact terms version and person; missing required consent blocks submission.
Holder, account, backing and controls are shown together; submit binds the reviewed version.

workflows.journey: Track application stage and next actor
workflows.acceptance: A pending screen names the missing information or responsible reviewer and preserves a safe status reference.
Required approval binds the payload; editing it invalidates approval and approval alone cannot issue the card.
Submitted, simulated approval and issued remain distinct; timeout triggers reconciliation with the same operation.
Show a safe simulated reason and next step; never present fictional checks as real underwriting.
A linked case preserves the original decision and evidence; request-for-review is not a changed outcome.

workflows.journey: Configure amount and date controls for virtual use
workflows.acceptance: Optional controls remain in the canonical request; unsupported restrictions are explicitly unavailable.
The request correlates its intended payment and produces at most one card despite repeated submission.
Only an actor authorized by the applicable holder/guardian/product policy can perform supported mock activation; issuance and activation remain separate.

workflows.journey: Replace a card with an explicit reason
workflows.acceptance: Replacement uses the same command family, links its predecessor and preserves obligations, usage and reward history.

workflows.journey: Track card fulfillment separately from approval
workflows.acceptance: Delivery pending/failed is explicit; a shipment or acknowledgment cannot silently activate the card.
Card closure blocks new authorizations while existing holds, clearing and disputes remain reconcilable.
Amounts use distinct labels for backing, pending purchases, obligations and availability; role scope is apparent.

workflows.journey: Inspect a pending versus posted purchase
workflows.acceptance: Status, dates and amount are consistent with durable events; pending activity is not final expense or reward.
Search/date/card filters retain context, enforce scope and distinguish no results from unavailable data.
Export preserves authorized scope, exact amounts and chosen filters; formula-like text is inert.
The statement reconciles to posted activity and identifies period, due obligations and corrections.
Requested/ready/failed states survive reload and give a safe retry without leaking private documents.
Show the actual obligation and authorized fictional source; durable confirmation distinguishes processing from applied.
Amount meaning, date and obligation are reviewed; execution rechecks live policy and follows a defined race policy.
Effective date and first execution are explicit; any current amount still due remains visible.
Server determines cancelability; a completion race returns the actual recorded outcome.
Scheduled, applied, failed and returned are distinct; returns use linked corrections.
A suspicious pending event can start a safety/support case without inventing a posted chargeback.

workflows.journey: Open and follow a transaction dispute
workflows.acceptance: One linked case shows reason, evidence and next step; status does not promise reimbursement.

workflows.journey: Withdraw a dispute with a reason
workflows.acceptance: Withdrawal is capability- and state-dependent, auditable, and does not erase existing financial effects.

workflows.journey: Understand rewards by stage and source
workflows.acceptance: Use Etail accrual/posting rules and one membership-year cap; reversals link to original accrual.

workflows.journey: Inspect and enroll in an eligible benefit
workflows.acceptance: Only an actually specified Etail benefit can be enrolled; absent product support remains a scored gap.
Recovery and revocation work through the one Identity integration; unverified passkey support remains visible as a gap.

workflows.journey: Read accessible statements and obtain help
workflows.acceptance: Keyboard and assistive reading can reach statement details and support; automated accessibility checks alone do not pass.

workflows.journey: Save and submit a merchant application
workflows.acceptance: One named Seller request retains draft/version; received status does not imply merchant approval.

workflows.journey: Add a location within an approved relationship
workflows.acceptance: Location, submitter and payee identities are explicit and cannot create an unrelated legal merchant.

workflows.journey: Review a batch of location requests
workflows.acceptance: Each item uses the same scoped command, has its own outcome and retries without duplicating successful items.
Material legal information uses a dedicated review path; submitted values stay separate from effective values.
Review names exact scope and destination; step-up and approval checks precede a tracked change operation.
Payments retain safe payer/request references and exact money; list queries enforce Seller/location scope.
Batch totals reconcile to included payments and retain both submitting and payee relationships.
Expected components and confirmed payout are distinct; unsettled amounts cannot be withdrawn or pledged.
Each fee/reserve/refund/adjustment has a source and status; unknown costs are never confirmed zero.

workflows.journey: Drill from settlement to an individual payment
workflows.acceptance: A stable correlation chain explains all included effects without exposing private issuer information.

workflows.journey: Search submissions by amount, date and location
workflows.acceptance: The date basis and filters are explicit; unauthorized location queries disclose no data.
Issued statements reconcile by period and currency; not-yet-issued differs from a zero-activity statement.
Lookup finds the linked financial effect within scope using safe references; case access is separately authorized.

workflows.journey: Inspect a dispute and reply deadline
workflows.acceptance: Transaction amount, disputed amount, case type and deadline source are distinct fields.

workflows.journey: Contest a claim with permitted evidence
workflows.acceptance: Response choices follow case/provider capability; stale deadlines and unsupported partial refund actions are checked.

workflows.journey: Accept a claim or reconcile a prior refund
workflows.acceptance: Before any credit, account for existing refunds/debits and refundable remainder to prevent duplicate reimbursement.

workflows.journey: Add evidence after an initial response
workflows.acceptance: Upload, validated, submitted and provider-accepted states are separate; failed processing is repairable.

workflows.journey: Review a closed dispute and financial outcome
workflows.acceptance: Case result and reconciled money remain distinguishable; unmatched effects stay in an exception queue.
Reports identify authorized scope, period, freshness and missing enrichment, with drill-down to source activity.
Unused/partly used allocations and genuine overages remain visible without creating new available capacity.
The report uses effective controls and committed usage, and links to a permitted control review.
Age is computed under the product calendar; a case assignment does not authorize debt or fee changes.
Only authorized accounts aggregate; separate currencies and pending/posted obligations remain identifiable.
Allocation totals match the source expense; recoding never edits posted financial journals.
Evidence is private, scoped and versioned; malformed or rejected files leave a recoverable task.
An independent eligible reviewer approves the exact allocation version; self-approval and stale payloads fail.
Versioned values and valid combinations are checked before export; historical classifications remain traceable.
The job reports accepted/rejected counts, actor and timing; failed/retried jobs cannot silently replace source history.
A private artifact records definition/version, source cutoff and row count, with totals reconciled to its scope.

workflows.journey: Save and rerun a report definition
workflows.acceptance: Saved filters and columns are versioned preferences; permissions are rechecked on every run and download.

workflows.journey: Find a scheduled or generated report
workflows.acceptance: Queued/generating/ready/failed/expired states are visible and a lost permission blocks old artifact access.
Priority uses actual reply deadlines; case type and current financial debit do not collapse into one status.

workflows.journey: Review case history and the next action
workflows.acceptance: Customer/internal/provider records have separate visibility and safe correlation; actions use owning domain commands.
An operator sees the safe failure reason, can request replacement and cannot fabricate provider acceptance.

workflows.journey: Audit pending and failed account changes
workflows.acceptance: Before/proposed/effective values and actor/status are distinguishable; a receipt alone cannot imply applied change.
Help retains authorized account/case context and actual service availability; support access does not grant money movement.

mandatory_gates.requirement: One issuing command, saved request and Add card form; replacement and virtual formats use the same ownership.
One financial ledger; balanced immutable postings with exact minor units and currency.
One server policy; scoped reads/commands/files/exports and immediate revocation.
Atomic shared backing across cards/accounts, payouts, refunds and pledges.
Stable business identities and unique effects despite retries, duplicate or out-of-order events.
Genuine late clearing reconciles after freeze/revocation without authorizing new activity.
PERSONAL, HOUSEHOLD, SELLER only; liability, sponsor, role and card format stay distinct.
Guardian-funded supervised spending creates no independent borrowing or child repayment bill.
Household sharing never exposes unrelated Personal/Seller totals or history.
Etail rates, membership years, rewards and one Premier cap retain source provenance; D14–D17 resolved for affected writes.
No secrets or real PAN/CVV/bank/KYB data in the sandbox; provider credentials remain behind adapters.
Money controls, task order, navigation and status are understandable on desktop/mobile with keyboard and assistive access.
Mock provider uses the same commands/events; real money is enforced off.
Practice purchase completes through durable events; no customer manual-clearing button or fabricated client success.
Account/card offboarding blocks new activity, explains outstanding obligations and preserves in-flight reconciliation/history.
Guest payments, QR/links, partial invoices and recurring mock collection remain retained Etail scope even outside Amex portal comparisons.
Sensitive adjustments/destination changes require explicit scope, current approval and payload binding.
Operations, economics and partner API/portal scope remains in backlog; no second generic CRUD/financial engine.
Meaningful PostgreSQL, provider replay, concurrency, contract, accessibility, browser, security and build checks pass for release SHA.
Fresh hosted resources, real hosted acceptance, feature review and public-release approval remain independent gates.

target_update_reason: User requested 100% and a better Etail experience. The existing 90 tasks and independent mandatory gates are preserved; target change does not award points.
